title: Why Promises?
description:
Promises are the cleanest and newest (not only) way to handle the situation of needing to ask a server somthing, which is typically done with a [HTTP Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods), using TypeScripts [fetch()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API) API. (Later course), which returns a promise.
Almost every time you use a promise it will be for I/O (when our code needs to interact with the outside world).
Common examples of I/O?
- HTTP requests. (I and O)
- Reading Files. (I)
- Using Bluetooth (I and 0)
- Printing to Console (O)

---
## Question:
Promises are the only way to write Async code in TypeScript.
